title: One Cocoon = 900m of Silk Thread — China Killed to Keep It Secret | China Travel Expert
description:
One silkworm cocoon unwinds into a single thread up to 900 metres long — and for thousands of years, China was the only place on Earth that knew how.

Sericulture was a state secret so valuable that an imperial decree made smuggling silkworms or their eggs out of the empire punishable by death; guards on the Silk Road checked travelers for them. It takes roughly 2,000 cocoons to weave a single silk dress. The monopoly finally broke around AD 550, when two monks reportedly carried silkworm eggs to the Byzantine emperor hidden inside hollow bamboo staves.

🧭 Expert Tip: In Suzhou — China's silk capital — the silk museums keep live silkworms and working looms, so you can watch a cocoon become thread in real time.

一颗蚕茧，能抽出九百米长的一根丝——这个秘密，中国守了几千年。
